subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical approval requests, and what cache key, lifetime, and decision set are acceptable?
rationale: The redundant billing path is source-proven, but caching a model reviewer result changes when a later exec request bypasses a fresh approval-boundary review.

options.title: Approve full-input per-reviewer memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside a reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results while leaving ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or billing evidence changes the tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-reviewer memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside a reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate from current blame and merged normalized auto-mode ownership for the exec approval cache decision.
